sources.title: Nemotron 3 VoiceChat model card
sources.evidence: Reopened the exact Markdown endpoint on October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200). It still identifies the March 16, 2026 early-access v1.0 release as a nominal 12B integrated full-duplex speech model, explicitly naming and linking the NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 language backbone. Architecture includes a Fast Conformer speech encoder and speech decoder/codec. It accepts and emits text and audio, lists the Evaluation License, describes training audio context of up to two minutes, and explicitly states it was not trained for reasoning or alignment. The function-calling reference is a training dataset, not a supported tool interface. It supplies no separate active-parameter count.

sources.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 VoiceChat Early Access Program
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200). The early-access program explicitly describes the model as 12B parameters with speech recognition, language modeling and speech generation integrated in one architecture. It advertises inspectable weights through access for qualified developers, not a separately verified public checkpoint. No active-parameter count is stated.

sources.title: NVIDIA Software and Model Evaluation License
sources.evidence: The agreement linked by the exact model card is the NVIDIA Software and Model Evaluation License, last modified February 26, 2025. It governs the delivered evaluation materials; the card separately identifies API Trial Service Terms for hosted API use.

sources.title: Original Nemotron VoiceChat NGC registry link
sources.evidence: The exact NGC destination linked by the March model card redirects to signout. Its corresponding public API request returned HTTP 401. No files or tensor headers for this exact release were accessed; this failure alone does not establish that weights are closed.

sources.title: NVIDIA NemotronLabs VoiceChat 11B model card
sources.evidence: Reopened the pinned card and current card on October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200). Both call the later public NemotronLabs VoiceChat model 11B, give August 3, 2026 as its release date, specify OpenMDW 1.1, and document a separate tool-output channel. These different specifications are not bound to the March 12B early-access checkpoint; neither its total nor its architecture details establish the original release's active count.

sources.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
sources.evidence: Freshly reread the full October 1 report revision and its architecture/training sections. The later NemotronLabs model uses NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-Base, a 600M speech encoder, and a TTS module with a 778M Gemma 3-based decoder plus 199M codec (977M combined). It has separate agent-text and function heads, an auxiliary RNN-T branch and independently trained STT/TTS components. These are later-model component totals, not an explicit active-parameter convention or an identity mapping to the March 12B model.

sources.title: SALM-Duplex: Efficient and Direct Duplex Modeling for Speech-to-Speech Language Model
sources.evidence: Freshly reread the full linked method paper, especially Section 3. Its experiment initializes TinyLlama-1.1B-chat with a 100M speech encoder and extends its vocabulary for speech tokens. This is a methodological predecessor with a different backbone, not an active-count disclosure for the March Nemotron VoiceChat checkpoint.

sources.title: Building NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Agents for Reasoning, Multimodal RAG, Voice, and Safety
sources.evidence: The March 24, 2026 article's authored VoiceChat section explicitly describes the early-access integrated speech model as 12B parameters, built on the Nemotron Nano v2 LLM with speech encoder and TTS decoder. The 12B active-per-pass statement elsewhere in this article describes Nemotron 3 Super, not VoiceChat; it cannot supply VoiceChat activity.

sources.title: NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 model card
sources.evidence: Retrieved the full original backbone card October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200). This is the exact named checkpoint linked from the March VoiceChat card. It establishes a nominal 9B hybrid language model and references the Nano 2 report, but supplies no explicit active-parameter count; its total alone is not an activity convention.

sources.title: NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 2: An Accurate and Efficient Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Reasoning Model
sources.evidence: Freshly reread the original Nano 2 report, including architecture and Section 4.4. The nominal 9B model is compressed from a 12B model by pruning full layers, FFN widths and embedding channels; the resulting model retains 56 layers. Its comparisons, architecture and pruning sections do not explicitly give an activated-parameter count for the named 9B backbone. The 12B pre-pruning language model is not VoiceChat's integrated 12B total.

sources.title: Audio Flamingo 3: Advancing Audio Intelligence with Fully Open Large Audio Language Models
sources.evidence: Read the original paper linked as the March VoiceChat TTS reference, including Section 3.1 and Appendix I. It explains a streaming decoder/codec and gives 644M for its three-layer MLP block, but no complete VoiceChat total or explicit active-parameter convention. The method reference does not identify an unchanged exact March speech-decoder checkpoint, so its component details cannot determine an integrated or per-phase active count.

sources.title: ST4TS: historical local inference measurements
sources.evidence: Freshly read the original hardware-benchmark page, exact Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 row and methodology. The row lists 9B total and 9B active alongside August 12, 2026 measurements for a community Q4_K_M checkpoint on an R9700. The page documents throughput benchmarking, but does not identify a source or counting method for this active-parameter figure. It is an unresolved independent lead, not accepted as an established active convention for the backbone or the March VoiceChat model.

sources.title: Untangling Input Language from Reasoning Language
sources.evidence: The search index exposes Table 26 with Nemotron-Nano-9B at 9B total/9B active, but the full primary PDF request encounters a browser-verification challenge. The same indexed table incorrectly labels GPT-OSS-20B as dense with 20B active, undermining its parameter convention. This unverified, internally suspect lead is not adopted.

name.note: Use the exact first-party early-access name, distinguishing it from the later NemotronLabs VoiceChat 11B release.

developer.note: Both official pages identify NVIDIA as the model developer.

family.note: The first-party model name and program identify the Nemotron family.

release_date.note: The model card explicitly dates the original NGC release March 16, 2026. This is an early-access evaluation release, not the later public NemotronLabs release.

open_weights.note: The official early-access program advertises inspectable weights but restricts hands-on access to qualified developers. Public availability of the exact March checkpoint was not verified; the original registry could not be read. The public later 11B checkpoint is not a substitute, and an access failure does not justify asserting closed weights. Clear the unsupported public-open assertion.

license.value: NVIDIA Software and Model Evaluation License
license.note: These are the exact card's terms for the model and NIM container. Hosted API trial terms are separate. Do not transfer OpenMDW 1.1 from the later NemotronLabs release.

parameters_b.note: Retain NVIDIA's explicit nominal 12B total for the integrated March 16 early-access model, independently repeated in its March 24 launch article. The identified 9B language backbone is a component; the later 11B NemotronLabs release does not replace this count. A tensor census is unnecessary to retain the published nominal specification.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh original-source review found no supported active count for the March model or its named 9B backbone. The newer Labs report supplies component totals for a different release; SALM-Duplex uses TinyLlama, and Audio Flamingo 3 is a TTS method reference. Directive4 lists 9B active for the backbone without parameter-count provenance, while an inaccessible OpenReview comparison has an erroneous GPT-OSS activity row; neither establishes a reliable convention. Do not equate the integrated 12B total or 9B backbone size with activity or invent phase counts.

architecture.note: The exact card labels the architecture hybrid Mamba/Transformer. It additionally identifies the Fast Conformer speech encoder and convolutional/Transformer speech decoder. This is an integrated speech model, not a claim that all components are the 9B language backbone.

context_window.note: The exact card documents training audio context of up to two minutes, not a maximum token context. Clear the unsupported 128,000-token assertion; neither the audio duration nor backbone context can be converted or transferred without an exact-model definition.

modalities.note: The card specifies text prompts and 16 kHz user speech inputs, with agent text, user transcription and 22.05 kHz generated speech outputs. Add the omitted audio output; no image or video modality is documented.

reasoning.note: The exact card explicitly states that this model was not trained for reasoning or alignment. Retain false for dedicated reasoning capability; this does not deny that it can answer questions requiring some reasoning.

tool_call.note: The March card mentions function-calling data in training but does not document a supported tool interface. The later Labs model explicitly adds a tool-output channel, but its identity is different. Clear the unsupported true value rather than infer either support or absence.

description.value: Early-access speech-to-speech model combining a Fast Conformer encoder, Nemotron Nano v2 language backbone and speech decoder for simultaneous listening and speaking.
description.note: Replace the unsupported visual-reasoning and agentic-workflow description with the exact model's documented duplex speech behavior and integrated components.

patch.notes: March 2026 early-access Nemotron 3 VoiceChat: NVIDIA reports 12B total parameters, including a named 9B Nano v2 language backbone. An active count is not disclosed. The later public 11B NemotronLabs release is distinct. Training audio context is up to two minutes; a token limit, public availability of the exact early-access weights and supported tool calling remain unverified.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter review retains the directly published nominal 12B integrated total from the exact March 16 card, early-access page and March 24 launch article. Active parameters remain undisclosed after reviewing the Nano 2 backbone, original speech-model methods, later NemotronLabs report and two insufficiently supported active-count leads. The later 11B model and predecessor/component totals are not substituted. The other twelve field assessments are preserved.
